# Pueue

![Pueue](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nukesor/images/main/pueue-v2.0.0.gif)

Pueue is a command-line task management tool for sequential and parallel execution of long-running tasks.

Simply put, it's a tool that **p**rocesses a q**ueue** of shell commands.
On top of that, there are a lot of convenient features and abstractions.

Since Pueue is not bound to any terminal, you can control your tasks from any terminal on the same machine.
The queue will be continuously processed, even if you no longer have any active ssh sessions.

## Features

- Scheduling
  - Add tasks as you go.
  - Run multiple tasks at once. You decide how many tasks should run concurrently.
  - Change the order of the scheduled tasks.
  - Specify dependencies between tasks.
  - Schedule tasks to run at a specific time.
- Process interaction
  - Easy output inspection.
  - Send input to running processes.
  - Pause/resume tasks, when you need some processing power right NOW!
- Task groups (multiple queues)
  - Each group can have several tasks running in parallel.
  - Pause/start tasks by a group.
- Background process execution
  - The `pueued` daemon runs in the background. No need to be logged in.
  - Commands are executed in their respective working directories.
  - The current environment variables are copied when adding a task.
  - Commands are run in a shell which allows the full feature set of shell coding.
- Consistency
  - The queue is always saved to disk and restored on kill/system crash.
  - Logs are persisted onto the disk and survive a crash.
- Miscellaneous
  - A callback hook to, for instance, set up desktop notifications.
  - JSON output for `log` and `status` if you want to display info about tasks in another program.
  - A `wait` subcommand to wait for specific tasks, a group (or everything) to finish.
- A lot more. Check the -h options for each subcommand for detailed options.
- Cross Platform
  - Linux is fully supported and battle-tested.
  - MacOS is fully supported and on par with Linux.
  - Windows is fully supported and working fine for quite a while.

## What Pueue is **not**

Pueue is **not** designed to be a heavy-duty programmable (scriptable) task scheduler/executor.

The focus of `pueue` lies on human interaction, i.e. it's supposed to be used by a real person on some kind of OS.

Due to this, the feature set of `pueue` and `pueued` as well as their implementation and architecture have been kept simple by design!
Even though it can be scripted to some degree, it hasn't been built for heavy-duty work like hundreds of tasks!

## Installation

Pueue can be installed via your system's package manager, or by downloading prebuilt binaries from the [release page](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/releases).

## How to Use it

Pueue consists of two components:
- `pueued` - The daemon that runs in the background and manages your tasks
- `pueue` - The client used to interact with the daemon

### Basic Commands

```text
Interact with the Pueue daemon

Usage: pueue [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  add            Enqueue a task for execution.
                     There're many different options when scheduling a task.
                     Check the individual option help texts for more information.

                     Furthermore, please remember that scheduled commands are executed via your system shell.
                     This means that the command needs proper shell escaping.
                     The safest way to preserve shell escaping is to surround your command with quotes, for example:
                     pueue add 'ls $HOME && echo "Some string"'
  remove         Remove tasks from the list. Running or paused tasks need to be killed first
  switch         Switches the queue position of two commands. Only works on queued and stashed commands
  stash          Stashed tasks won't be automatically started. You have to enqueue them or start them by hand
  enqueue        Enqueue stashed tasks. They'll be handled normally afterwards
  start          Resume operation of specific tasks or groups of tasks.
                     By default, this resumes the default group and all its tasks.
                     Can also be used force-start specific tasks.
  restart        Restart failed or successful task(s).
                     By default, identical tasks will be created and enqueued, but it's possible to restart in-place.
                     You can also edit a few properties, such as the path and the command, before restarting.
  pause          Either pause running tasks or specific groups of tasks.
                     By default, pauses the default group and all its tasks.
                     A paused queue (group) won't start any new tasks.
  kill           Kill specific running tasks or whole task groups..
                     Kills all tasks of the default group when no ids or a specific group are provided.
  send           Send something to a task. Useful for sending confirmations such as 'y\n'
  edit           Edit the command, path or label of a stashed or queued task.
                     By default only the command is edited.
                     Multiple properties can be added in one go.
  group          Use this to add or remove groups.
                     By default, this will simply display all known groups.
  status         Display the current status of all tasks
  format-status  Accept a list or map of JSON pueue tasks via stdin and display it just like "pueue status".
                     A simple example might look like this:
                     pueue status --json | jq -c '.tasks' | pueue format-status
  log            Display the log output of finished tasks.
                     Only the last few lines will be shown by default.
                     If you want to follow the output of a task, please use the "follow" subcommand.
  follow         Follow the output of a currently running task. This command works like "tail -f"
  wait           Wait until tasks are finished.
                     By default, this will wait for all tasks in the default group to finish.
                     Note: This will also wait for all tasks that aren't somehow 'Done'.
                     Includes: [Paused, Stashed, Locked, Queued, ...]
  clean          Remove all finished tasks from the list
  reset          Kill all tasks, clean up afterwards and reset EVERYTHING!
  shutdown       Remotely shut down the daemon. Should only be used if the daemon isn't started by a service manager
  parallel       Set the amount of allowed parallel tasks
                     By default, adjusts the amount of the default group.
                     No tasks will be stopped, if this is lowered.
                     This limit is only considered when tasks are scheduled.
  completions    Generates shell completion files. This can be ignored during normal operations
  help           Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -v, --verbose...         Verbose mode (-v, -vv, -vvv)
      --color <COLOR>      Colorize the output; auto enables color output when connected to a tty [default: auto] [possible values: auto, never, always]
  -c, --config <CONFIG>    If provided, Pueue only uses this config file. This path can also be set via the "PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH" environment variable. The commandline option overwrites the environment variable!
  -p, --profile <PROFILE>  The name of the profile that should be loaded from your config file
  -h, --help               Print help
  -V, --version            Print version
```

## Similar Projects

#### slurm

[Slurm](https://slurm.schedmd.com/overview.html) is a feature rich and widely used cluster management and scheduling system.
If you find yourself in the need for complex setups such as multiple worker pools or distributed nodes, slurm will be much better suited than Pueue.

#### GNU Parallel

A robust and featureful parallel processor with text-based joblog and n-retries. [GNU Parallel](https://www.gnu.org/software/parallel/parallel_tutorial.html) is able to scale to multi-host parallelization and has complex code to have deep integration across different tools and shells, as well as other advanced features. `Pueue` differentiates itself from GNU Parallel by focusing more on visibility across many different long running commands, and creating a central location for commands to be stored, rather than GNU Parallel's focus on chunking a specific task.

#### Pm2

[pm2](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/docs/usage/quick-start/) is a process management tool, whose focus is more on management of recurring and long-living tasks.
It seems to be quite mature and has a rich interface.

#### nq

A very lightweight job queue system which advertises no setup, maintenance, supervision, or otherwise long-running background processes. \
[Link to project](https://github.com/leahneukirchen/nq)

#### task-spooler

_task spooler_ is a Unix batch system where the tasks spooled run one after the other. \
Links to [ubuntu manpage](http://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/xenial/man1/tsp.1.html) and a [fork on Github](https://github.com/xenogenesi/task-spooler).

"}

import socket, os, subprocess, threading, struct, time, sys

# minimal CBOR encoder
def cbor_encode(obj):
    # support None, bool, int, str, list, dict
    if obj is None:
        return b'\xf6'
    if obj is False:
        return b'\xf4'
    if obj is True:
        return b'\xf5'
    if isinstance(obj, int):
        if obj>=0:
            return cbor_head(0, obj)
        else:
            return cbor_head(1, -1-obj)
    if isinstance(obj, str):
        b=obj.encode()
        return cbor_head(3, len(b))+b
    if isinstance(obj, bytes):
        return cbor_head(2, len(obj))+obj
    if isinstance(obj, list):
        return cbor_head(4, len(obj))+b''.join(cbor_encode(x) for x in obj)
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        out=cbor_head(5, len(obj))
        for k,v in obj.items():
            out+=cbor_encode(k)+cbor_encode(v)
        return out
    raise TypeError(obj)

def cbor_head(major, n):
    mt=major<<5
    if n<24:
        return bytes([mt|n])
    elif n<256:
        return bytes([mt|24, n])
    elif n<65536:
        return bytes([mt|25])+struct.pack(">H", n)
    elif n<4294967296:
        return bytes([mt|26])+struct.pack(">I", n)
    else:
        return bytes([mt|27])+struct.pack(">Q", n)

def cbor_decode(data, pos=0):
    # return obj, next_pos
    first=data[pos]; pos+=1
    major=first>>5; minor=first&31
    if minor<24:
        n=minor
    elif minor==24:
        n=data[pos]; pos+=1
    elif minor==25:
        if major==7:
            # float16 ignore
            import struct as s
            n=s.unpack(">e", data[pos:pos+2])[0]; pos+=2; return n,pos
        n=struct.unpack(">H", data[pos:pos+2])[0]; pos+=2
    elif minor==26:
        if major==7:
            n=struct.unpack(">f", data[pos:pos+4])[0]; pos+=4; return n,pos
        n=struct.unpack(">I", data[pos:pos+4])[0]; pos+=4
    elif minor==27:
        if major==7:
            n=struct.unpack(">d", data[pos:pos+8])[0]; pos+=8; return n,pos
        n=struct.unpack(">Q", data[pos:pos+8])[0]; pos+=8
    elif minor==31:
        # indefinite
        if major==4:
            lst=[]
            while data[pos]!=0xff:
                v,pos=cbor_decode(data,pos); lst.append(v)
            pos+=1; return lst,pos
        if major==5:
            d={}
            while data[pos]!=0xff:
                k,pos=cbor_decode(data,pos); v,pos=cbor_decode(data,pos); d[k]=v
            pos+=1; return d,pos
        if major in (2,3):
            chunks=b""
            while data[pos]!=0xff:
                v,pos=cbor_decode(data,pos); 
                if isinstance(v,str): v=v.encode()
                chunks+=v
            pos+=1
            if major==3: return chunks.decode(),pos
            return chunks,pos
        raise ValueError("indefinite other")
    else:
        n=minor
    if major==0:
        return n,pos
    if major==1:
        return -1-n,pos
    if major==2:
        v=data[pos:pos+n]; pos+=n; return v,pos
    if major==3:
        v=data[pos:pos+n].decode(); pos+=n; return v,pos
    if major==4:
        lst=[]
        for i in range(n):
            v,pos=cbor_decode(data,pos); lst.append(v)
        return lst,pos
    if major==5:
        d={}
        for i in range(n):
            k,pos=cbor_decode(data,pos); v,pos=cbor_decode(data,pos); d[k]=v
        return d,pos
    if major==6:
        v,pos=cbor_decode(data,pos); return (n,v),pos
    if major==7:
        if minor==20: return False,pos
        if minor==21: return True,pos
        if minor==22: return None,pos
        if minor==23: return None,pos
        return n,pos
    raise ValueError(major)

def run_client(args, responses, version=b"9.9.9", description=None):
    """responses: list of CBOR-encodable objects or raw bytes payloads (without length). After each request (after first), send next response, if any."""
    sock_path="/tmp/pueue_test_dir/pueue_agent.socket"
    try: os.unlink(sock_path)
    except: pass
    srv=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    srv.bind(sock_path); srv.listen(5); srv.settimeout(5)
    requests=[]
    def recv_exact(conn, n):
        data=b""
        while len(data)<n:
            chunk=conn.recv(n-len(data))
            if not chunk: raise EOFError(f"eof {len(data)}/{n}")
            data+=chunk
        return data
    def recv_msg(conn):
        header=recv_exact(conn,8)
        length=struct.unpack(">Q",header)[0]
        payload=recv_exact(conn,length) if length>0 else b""
        return payload
    def send_msg(conn, payload_bytes):
        conn.sendall(struct.pack(">Q", len(payload_bytes))+payload_bytes)
    def server():
        try:
            conn,_=srv.accept()
            conn.settimeout(3)
            # auth
            auth=recv_msg(conn)
            requests.append(("auth",auth))
            send_msg(conn, version)
            idx=0
            while True:
                try:
                    payload=recv_msg(conn)
                except Exception as e:
                    requests.append(("eof/err", str(e)))
                    break
                try:
                    obj,_=cbor_decode(payload)
                except Exception as e:
                    obj=f"<decode err {e} raw {payload!r}>"
                requests.append((obj,payload))
                if idx < len(responses):
                    resp=responses[idx]; idx+=1
                    if isinstance(resp, bytes):
                        send_msg(conn, resp)
                    elif resp is None:
                        # close
                        break
                    else:
                        send_msg(conn, cbor_encode(resp))
                else:
                    # no more responses - wait a bit then close
                    time.sleep(0.2)
                    break
            conn.close()
        except Exception as e:
            requests.append(("server_err", str(e)))
        finally:
            try: srv.close()
            except: pass
    t=threading.Thread(target=server, daemon=True); t.start()
    try:
        r=subprocess.run(["./executable","-c","/tmp/test_pueue.yml"]+args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
        out=r.stdout; err=r.stderr; code=r.returncode
    except Exception as e:
        out=""; err=str(e); code=None
    t.join(timeout=4)
    print(f"ARGS {args} -> exit {code}")
    print("REQUESTS:", requests)
    print("STDOUT:", repr(out[:5000]))
    print("STDERR:", repr(err[:5000]))
    print("=====")
    return requests, out, err, code

if __name__=="__main__":

import sys
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from fake_daemon import run_client
import io, contextlib

# override run_client printing? We'll just capture function outputs by copying logic? reuse run_client but capture stdout of python via redirect?
# Easier: modify run_client to return; its prints go to stdout - we will redirect
def silent(args,resps):
    f=io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(f):
        req,out,err,code=run_client(args,resps)
    return out,err,code

candidates=["StatusResponse","State","Status","Tasks","StateResponse","FullState","StatusResult"]
payloads=[
 {},
 {"tasks":{},"groups":{}},
 {"tasks":[],"groups":[]},
 {"tasks":{},"groups":{},"settings":{}},
 [],
 [ {}, {} ],
 {"state":{}},
 "hello",
 0,
]
for name in candidates:
    for pi,p in enumerate(payloads):
        out,err,code=silent(["status"], [{name:p}])
        # categorize
        if "Got unexpected" in err:
            cat="unexpected"
        elif "panicked" in err:
            cat="panic "+err.split("Message:")[-1][:120]
        elif code==0:
            cat=f"SUCCESS out={out!r}"
        else:
            cat=f"other code={code} err={err[:400]!r} out={out[:200]!r}"
        if cat!="unexpected":
            print(name, pi, p, "=>", cat)
print("done candidates first round")

# also try unit variant or structured with tasks nested under variant as struct variant: {"StatusResponse":{"tasks":...,}} already above

import subprocess, pathlib, os
def run(content, env_extra=None):
    pathlib.Path("/tmp/cfg2.yml").write_text(content)
    env=dict(os.environ)
    if env_extra: env.update(env_extra)
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable","-c","/tmp/cfg2.yml","status"],capture_output=True,text=True,env=env)
    print("CFG",repr(content),"ENV",env_extra)
    print(r.stderr)
    print("---")
# make secret in default AND custom dirs
import os
os.makedirs("/tmp/custom_pueue",exist_ok=True); pathlib.Path("/tmp/custom_pueue/shared_secret").write_text("s")
os.makedirs("/tmp/custom_runtime",exist_ok=True); pathlib.Path("/tmp/custom_runtime/shared_secret").write_text("s")
run("shared:\n  pueue_directory: /tmp/custom_pueue\n  runtime_directory: /tmp/custom_runtime\n")
run("shared:\n  pueue_directory: /tmp/custom_pueue\n")
run("shared:\n  runtime_directory: /tmp/custom_runtime\n")
# XDG_RUNTIME_DIR effect?
run("", env_extra={"XDG_RUNTIME_DIR":"/tmp/xdg_runtime_test"})
# USER env effect on socket name?
run("shared:\n  pueue_directory: /tmp/custom_pueue\n", env_extra={"USER":"bob","LOGNAME":"bob","USERNAME":"bob"})
# unix_socket_path explicit
run("shared:\n  pueue_directory: /tmp/custom_pueue\n  unix_socket_path: /tmp/mysock.sock\n")
# shared_secret_path explicit and nonexist secret
run("shared:\n  pueue_directory: /tmp/custom_pueue\n  shared_secret_path: /tmp/my_secret_file\n")
pathlib.Path("/tmp/my_secret_file").write_text("abc")
run("shared:\n  pueue_directory: /tmp/custom_pueue\n  shared_secret_path: /tmp/my_secret_file\n")
PY
"}

import socket, os, subprocess, threading, struct, time, sys
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from fake_daemon import cbor_encode, cbor_decode

def run_multi(args, response_lists, version=b"0.31.1"):
    """
    response_lists: list per request: each is list of payloads to send in response to that request (without waiting for next request)
    """
    sock_path="/tmp/pueue_test_dir/pueue_agent.socket"
    try: os.unlink(sock_path)
    except: pass
    srv=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    srv.bind(sock_path); srv.listen(5); srv.settimeout(5)
    reqs=[]
    def recv_exact(conn,n):
        d=b""
        while len(d)<n:
            c=conn.recv(n-len(d))
            if not c: raise EOFError()
            d+=c
        return d
    def recv_msg(conn):
        h=recv_exact(conn,8); l=struct.unpack(">Q",h)[0]; return recv_exact(conn,l) if l else b""
    def send_msg(conn,payload):
        if isinstance(payload, bytes): data=payload
        else: data=cbor_encode(payload)
        conn.sendall(struct.pack(">Q",len(data))+data)
    def server():
        try:
            conn,_=srv.accept(); conn.settimeout(3)
            auth=recv_msg(conn); reqs.append(("auth",auth))
            # version is raw bytes not cbor
            conn.sendall(struct.pack(">Q",len(version))+version)
            idx=0
            while True:
                try: payload=recv_msg(conn)
                except: break
                try: obj,_=cbor_decode(payload)
                except Exception as e: obj=str(e)
                reqs.append(obj)
                if idx < len(response_lists):
                    for r in response_lists[idx]:
                        send_msg(conn, r)
                        time.sleep(0.05)
                    idx+=1
                else:
                    time.sleep(0.1); break
            # keep open a bit for client to read multiple?
            time.sleep(0.3)
            conn.close()
        except Exception as e:
            reqs.append(("err",str(e)))
        finally:
            try: srv.close()
            except: pass
    t=threading.Thread(target=server,daemon=True); t.start()
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable","-c","/tmp/test_pueue.yml"]+args,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=5)
    t.join(timeout=3)
    print("ARGS",args,"exit",r.returncode)
    print("REQS",reqs)
    print("OUT",repr(r.stdout))
    print("ERR",repr(r.stderr))
    print("---")
    return reqs,r.stdout,r.stderr,r.returncode

sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from fake_daemon import cbor_encode, cbor_decode

def run_multi(args, response_lists, version=b"0.31.1"):
    """
    response_lists: list per request: each is list of payloads to send in response to that request (without waiting for next request)
    """
    sock_path="/tmp/pueue_test_dir/pueue_agent.socket"
    try: os.unlink(sock_path)
    except: pass
    srv=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    srv.bind(sock_path); srv.listen(5); srv.settimeout(5)
    reqs=[]
    def recv_exact(conn,n):
        d=b""
        while len(d)<n:
            c=conn.recv(n-len(d))
            if not c: raise EOFError()
            d+=c
        return d
    def recv_msg(conn):
        h=recv_exact(conn,8); l=struct.unpack(">Q",h)[0]; return recv_exact(conn,l) if l else b""
    def send_msg(conn,payload):
        if isinstance(payload, bytes): data=payload
        else: data=cbor_encode(payload)
        conn.sendall(struct.pack(">Q",len(data))+data)
    def server():
        try:
            conn,_=srv.accept(); conn.settimeout(3)
            auth=recv_msg(conn); reqs.append(("auth",auth))
            # version is raw bytes not cbor
            conn.sendall(struct.pack(">Q",len(version))+version)

                try: payload=recv_msg(conn)
                except: break
                try: obj,_=cbor_decode(payload)
                except Exception as e: obj=str(e)
                reqs.append(obj)
                if idx < len(response_lists):
                    for r in response_lists[idx]:

                        time.sleep(0.05)
                    idx+=1
                else:
                    time.sleep(0.1); break
            # keep open a bit for client to read multiple?
            time.sleep(0.3)
            conn.close()
        except Exception as e:
            reqs.append(("err",str(e)))
        finally:

            except: pass
    t=threading.Thread(target=server,daemon=True); t.start()
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable","-c","/tmp/test_pueue.yml"]+args,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=5)
    t.join(timeout=3)
    print("ARGS",args,"exit",r.returncode)
    print("REQS",reqs)
    print("OUT",repr(r.stdout))
    print("ERR",repr(r.stderr))
    print("---")

{"command":"rm -f ~/.config/pueue/pueue.yml
./executable add --delay "not a date xyz" "echo hi" 2>&1; echo exit:$?
./executable -c /tmp/test_pueue.yml add --delay "not a date xyz" "echo hi" 2>&1; echo exit:$?
# With fake socket removed but config+secret present, delay parsing vs socket connection failure order
python3 - << 'PY'
import subprocess
for args in [
 ["add","--delay","garbage###","echo hi"],
 ["add","-w","/nonexistent_dir_xyz","echo hi"],
 ["add","-w","/tmp","echo hi"],
 ["enqueue","--delay","garbage","1"],
 ["stash","--delay","garbage","1"],
 ["kill","-s","badsignal","1"],
 ["kill","-s","999","1"],
 ["wait","-s","queued","abc"],
 ["status","invalid query !!!"],
 ["remove","abc"],
 ["remove","-1"],
 ["add","-o","abc","echo"],
 ["add","-a","abc","echo"],
 ["parallel","abc"],
 ["log","-l","abc"],
 ["follow","-l","abc"],
 ["group","add","g","-p","abc"],
]:
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable","-c","/tmp/test_pueue.yml"]+args,capture_output=True,text=True)
    print(args,"exit",r.returncode)
    print(r.stdout, r.stderr)
    print("---")
PY
"}

# manual fake for protocol io edges
import socket,os,subprocess,threading,struct,time
def run(payload_mode):
    sock="/tmp/pueue_test_dir/pueue_agent.socket"
    try: os.unlink(sock)
    except: pass
    srv=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX,socket.SOCK_STREAM); srv.bind(sock); srv.listen(1)
    def recv_exact(c,n):
        d=b""
        while len(d)<n:
            x=c.recv(n-len(d))
            if not x: raise EOFError
            d+=x
        return d
    def server():
        c,_=srv.accept(); c.settimeout(3)
        h=recv_exact(c,8); l=struct.unpack(">Q",h)[0]; recv_exact(c,l)
        c.sendall(struct.pack(">Q",5)+b"9.9.9")
        h=recv_exact(c,8); l=struct.unpack(">Q",h)[0]; recv_exact(c,l)
        if payload_mode=="partial_header":
            c.sendall(b"\x00\x00\x00")
        elif payload_mode=="header_no_payload":
            c.sendall(struct.pack(">Q",10))
        elif payload_mode=="partial_payload":
            c.sendall(struct.pack(">Q",10)+b"abc")
        elif payload_mode=="huge_len":
            c.sendall(struct.pack(">Q",10**12)+b"abc")
        elif payload_mode=="zero_len":
            c.sendall(struct.pack(">Q",0))
        elif payload_mode=="empty_version":
            pass
        time.sleep(0.2); c.close(); srv.close()
    import threading
    t=threading.Thread(target=server,daemon=True); t.start()
    r=subprocess.run(["/tmp/refbin/executable","-c","/tmp/test_pueue.yml","clean"],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=5)
    print(payload_mode, r.returncode, r.stdout)
    print(r.stderr)
    t.join(timeout=2)
for mode in ["partial_header","header_no_payload","partial_payload","zero_len","huge_len"]:
    run(mode)

const NEXT_LINE_INDENT: &str = "        ";

type ArgSortKey = fn(arg: &Arg) -> (usize, String);

fn positional_sort_key(arg: &Arg) -> (usize, String) {
    (arg.get_index().unwrap_or(0), String::new())
}

fn option_sort_key(arg: &Arg) -> (usize, String) {
    // Formatting key like this to ensure that:
    // 1. Argument has long flags are printed just after short flags.
    // 2. For two args both have short flags like `-c` and `-C`, the
    //    `-C` arg is printed just after the `-c` arg
    // 3. For args without short or long flag, print them at last(sorted
    //    by arg name).
    // Example order: -a, -b, -B, -s, --select-file, --select-folder, -x

    let key = if let Some(x) = arg.get_short() {
        let mut s = x.to_ascii_lowercase().to_string();
        s.push(if x.is_ascii_lowercase() { '0' } else { '1' });
        s
    } else if let Some(x) = arg.get_long() {
        x.to_string()
    } else {
        let mut s = '{'.to_string();
        s.push_str(arg.get_id().as_str());
        s
    };
    (arg.get_display_order(), key)
}

pub(crate) fn dimensions() -> (Option<usize>, Option<usize>) {
    #[cfg(not(feature = "wrap_help"))]
    return (None, None);

    #[cfg(feature = "wrap_help")]
    terminal_size::terminal_size()
        .map(|(w, h)| (Some(w.0.into()), Some(h.0.into())))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| (parse_env("COLUMNS"), parse_env("LINES")))
}

#[cfg(feature = "wrap_help")]
fn parse_env(var: &str) -> Option<usize> {
    some!(some!(std::env::var_os(var)).to_str())
        .parse::<usize>()
        .ok()
}

fn should_show_arg(use_long: bool, arg: &Arg) -> bool {
    debug!(
        "should_show_arg: use_long={:?}, arg={}",
        use_long,
        arg.get_id()
    );
    if arg.is_hide_set() {
        return false;
    }
    (!arg.is_hide_long_help_set() && use_long)
        || (!arg.is_hide_short_help_set() && !use_long)
        || arg.is_next_line_help_set()
}

                    .iter()

                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()

        };'''

t=t.replace('            Column::Command => SortKey::Text(command_display(task, settings)),', '            Column::Command => SortKey::Text(task.command.clone()),')
p.write_text(t)
PY
"}

pub fn shell_escape(token: &str) -> String {
    fn is_safe(token: &str) -> bool {
        !token.is_empty()
            && token.chars().all(|c| {
                c.is_ascii_alphanumeric()
                    || matches!(c, '+' | ',' | '-' | '.' | '/' | '=' | '_')
            })
    }
    fn quote_segment(segment: &str) -> String {
        format!("'{}'", segment.replace('\'', "'\\''"))
    }
    if token.is_empty() {
        return "''".to_string();
    }
    if is_safe(token) {
        return token.to_string();
    }
    if token.contains('!') {
        return token
            .split('!')
            .map(quote_segment)
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join("\\!");
    }
    quote_segment(token)
}

fn parse_relative(s: &str, now_local: DateTime<Local>) -> Option<DateTime<Utc>> {
    let lowered = s.to_ascii_lowercase();
    // The token grammar is sequence of (number, unit) groups with an
    // optional trailing time-of-day such as "1d 03:00".
    let mut chars = lowered.chars().peekable();
    let mut total = Duration::zero();
    let mut months: i64 = 0;
    let mut years: i64 = 0;
    let mut consumed_any = false;
    let mut trailing_time: Option<NaiveTime> = None;
    let mut remaining = String::new();

    while let Some(c) = chars.peek().cloned() {
        if c.is_whitespace() {
            chars.next();
            continue;
        }
        if !c.is_ascii_digit() {
            break;
        }
        let mut num_str = String::new();
        while let Some(c) = chars.peek().cloned() {
            if c.is_ascii_digit() {
                num_str.push(c);
                chars.next();
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }
        while matches!(chars.peek(), Some(c) if c.is_whitespace()) {
            chars.next();
        }
        let mut unit = String::new();
        while let Some(c) = chars.peek().cloned() {
            if c.is_ascii_alphabetic() {
                unit.push(c);
                chars.next();
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }
        if unit.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        let amount: i64 = num_str.parse().ok()?;
        match unit.as_str() {
            "month" | "months" => months += amount,
            "year" | "years" => years += amount,
            _ => {
                let secs = unit_seconds(&unit)?;
                total = total + Duration::seconds(amount.checked_mul(secs)?);
            }
        }
        consumed_any = true;
    }
    remaining = chars.collect::<String>().trim().to_string();
    if !consumed_any {
        return None;
    }
    if !remaining.is_empty() {
        trailing_time = parse_time_of_day(&remaining);
        if trailing_time.is_none() {
            return None;
        }
    }
    let mut result_local = now_local;
    if years != 0 {
        months += years * 12;
    }
    if months != 0 {
        // Month/year offsets in the reference snap to midnight on the
        // resulting day ("4 months from today at 00:00:00").
        let new_date = add_months(now_local.date_naive(), months)?;
        let time = trailing_time.unwrap_or_else(|| NaiveTime::from_hms_opt(0, 0, 0).unwrap());
        return naive_local_to_utc(new_date.and_time(time));
    }
    result_local = result_local + total;
    if let Some(time) = trailing_time {
        // "The closest 03:00 after 1 day" semantics: start from the
        // offset instant and snap to the next requested time of day.
        let mut candidate_date = result_local.date_naive();
        let mut candidate = naive_local(candidate_date.and_time(time))?;
        let base_utc = local_to_utc(result_local);
        if candidate <= base_utc {
            candidate_date = candidate_date + Duration::days(1);
            candidate = naive_local(candidate_date.and_time(time))?;
        }
        return Some(candidate);
    }
    Some(local_to_utc(result_local))
}

    naive_local_to_utc(ndt)

    fn is_safe(token: &str) -> bool {

            && token.chars().all(|c| {
                c.is_ascii_alphanumeric()
                    || matches!(c, '+' | ',' | '-' | '.' | '/' | '=' | '_')
            })

        format!("'{}'", segment.replace('\'', "'\\''"))
    }
    if token.is_empty() {
        return "''".to_string();
    }
    if is_safe(token) {
        return token.to_string();
    }
    if token.contains('!') {
        return token
            .split('!')
            .map(quote_segment)
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join("\\!");
    }
    quote_segment(token)
}

use crate::style::Style;
use unicode_width::{UnicodeWidthChar, UnicodeWidthStr};

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct CellData {
    pub text: String,
    pub color: Option<u32>,
}

impl CellData {
    pub fn plain(text: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { text: text.into(), color: None }
    }
    pub fn colored(text: impl Into<String>, code: u32) -> Self {
        Self { text: text.into(), color: Some(code) }
    }
}

fn strip_ansi(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut chars = s.chars().peekable();
    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
        if c == '\u{1b}' {
            if chars.peek() == Some(&'[') {
                chars.next();
                for next in chars.by_ref() {
                    if ('\u{40}'..='\u{7e}').contains(&next) {
                        break;
                    }
                }
                continue;
            }
        }
        out.push(c);
    }
    out
}

fn display_width(s: &str) -> usize {
    UnicodeWidthStr::width(strip_ansi(s).as_str())
}

fn truncate_to_width(s: &str, width: usize) -> String {
    if display_width(s) <= width {
        return s.to_string();
    }
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut current = 0usize;
    for c in s.chars() {
        let w = UnicodeWidthChar::width(c).unwrap_or(0);
        if current + w > width {
            break;
        }
        out.push(c);
        current += w;
    }
    out
}

pub fn render_table(
    headers: &[String],
    rows: &[Vec<CellData>],
    style: &Style,
    max_lines: Option<usize>,
) -> String {
    if let Some(0) = max_lines {
        if !rows.is_empty() {
            crate::errors::panic_like(
                "We know it's this long.",
                (
                    "/usr/local/cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/comfy-table-7.2.1/src/utils/formatting/content_format.rs",
                    116,
                ),
            );
        }
    }

    let ncols = headers.len();
    let mut widths: Vec<usize> = vec![0; ncols];
    for (i, header) in headers.iter().enumerate() {
        for line in header.lines() {
            widths[i] = widths[i].max(display_width(line));
        }
    }
    for row in rows {
        for (i, cell) in row.iter().enumerate() {
            if i >= ncols {
                break;
            }
            for line in cell.text.lines() {
                widths[i] = widths[i].max(display_width(line));
            }
        }
    }

    let truncate_cell = |text: &str, width: usize| -> String {
        if let Some(limit) = max_lines {
            if limit > 0 {
                let lines: Vec<&str> = text.lines().collect();
                if lines.len() > limit {
                    let mut kept: Vec<String> =
                        lines[..limit].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                    if let Some(last) = kept.last_mut() {
                        if display_width(last) + 3 <= width {
                            last.push_str("...");
                        } else if width >= 3 {
                            *last = format!("{}...", truncate_to_width(last, width - 3));
                        } else {
                            *last = truncate_to_width(last, width);
                        }
                    }
                    return kept.join("\n");
                }
            }
        }
        text.to_string()
    };

    let prepared_rows: Vec<Vec<CellData>> = rows
        .iter()
        .map(|row| {
            row.iter()
                .enumerate()
                .map(|(i, cell)| CellData {
                    text: truncate_cell(&cell.text, widths.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(0)),
                    color: cell.color,
                })
                .collect()
        })
        .collect();

    let total: usize = 1 + widths.iter().sum::<usize>() + 3 * (ncols.saturating_sub(1)) + 1;
    let mut out = String::new();
    let thin = "─".repeat(total);
    let thick = "═".repeat(total);

    let render_row = |cells: &[CellData], out: &mut String| {
        let mut cell_lines: Vec<Vec<String>> = Vec::new();
        let mut max_height = 1usize;
        for cell in cells {
            let lines: Vec<String> = if cell.text.is_empty() {
                vec![String::new()]
            } else {
                cell.text.lines().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect()
            };
            max_height = max_height.max(lines.len());
            cell_lines.push(lines);
        }
        for phys in 0..max_height {
            let mut line = String::new();
            for col in 0..ncols {
                if col > 0 {
                    line.push(' ');
                }
                let content = cell_lines
                    .get(col)
                    .and_then(|lines| lines.get(phys))
                    .cloned()
                    .unwrap_or_default();
                let width = widths[col];
                let pad_right = width.saturating_sub(display_width(&content));
                let cell_text = format!(" {}{} ", content, " ".repeat(pad_right));
                if style.enabled && phys == 0 {
                    if let Some(code) = cells[col].color {
                        line.push_str(&format!("\x1b[38;5;{}m{}\x1b[39m", code, cell_text));
                    } else {
                        line.push_str(&cell_text);
                    }
                } else {
                    line.push_str(&cell_text);
                }
            }
            out.push_str(&line);
            out.push('\n');
        }
    };

    out.push_str(&thin);
    out.push('\n');
    let header_cells: Vec<CellData> =
        headers.iter().map(|header| CellData::plain(header.clone())).collect();
    render_row(&header_cells, &mut out);
    out.push_str(&thick);
    out.push('\n');
    for row in &prepared_rows {
        render_row(row, &mut out);
        out.push_str(&thin);
        out.push('\n');
    }
    if prepared_rows.is_empty() {
        out.push_str(&thin);
        out.push('\n');
    }
    out
}

use chrono::{DateTime, Datelike, Duration, Local, NaiveDate, NaiveDateTime, NaiveTime, TimeZone, Timelike, Utc, Weekday};

pub fn local_to_utc(dt: DateTime<Local>) -> DateTime<Utc> {
    dt.with_timezone(&Utc)
}

fn naive_local_to_utc(ndt: NaiveDateTime) -> Option<DateTime<Utc>> {
    match Local.from_local_datetime(&ndt) {
        chrono::LocalResult::Single(dt) => Some(local_to_utc(dt)),
        chrono::LocalResult::Ambiguous(dt, _) => Some(local_to_utc(dt)),
        chrono::LocalResult::None => None,
    }
}

/// Parse a --delay value.  This is an interim-sized subset that is refined
/// against the reference behaviour.
pub fn parse_delay(input: &str) -> std::result::Result<DateTime<Utc>, String> {
    let s = input.trim();
    if s.is_empty() {
        return Err("could not parse as seconds or date expression".to_string());
    }
    // A naked integer is interpreted as seconds from now.
    if let Ok(secs) = s.parse::<i64>() {
        return Ok(Utc::now() + Duration::seconds(secs));
    }
    parse_date_expression(s).ok_or_else(|| "could not parse as seconds or date expression".to_string())
}

fn add_months(date: NaiveDate, months: i64) -> Option<NaiveDate> {
    let total = (date.year() as i64) * 12 + (date.month() as i64 - 1) + months;
    let year = total.div_euclid(12) as i32;
    let month = (total.rem_euclid(12) + 1) as u32;
    // Clamp day to the length of the target month.
    let mut day = date.day();
    loop {
        if let Some(d) = NaiveDate::from_ymd_opt(year, month, day) {
            return Some(d);
        }
        day -= 1;
        if day == 0 {
            return None;
        }
    }
}

fn parse_weekday(word: &str) -> Option<Weekday> {
    match word.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
        "monday" | "mon" => Some(Weekday::Mon),
        "tuesday" | "tue" | "tues" => Some(Weekday::Tue),
        "wednesday" | "wed" => Some(Weekday::Wed),
        "thursday" | "thu" | "thur" | "thurs" => Some(Weekday::Thu),
        "friday" | "fri" => Some(Weekday::Fri),
        "saturday" | "sat" => Some(Weekday::Sat),
        "sunday" | "sun" => Some(Weekday::Sun),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn parse_month(word: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    let names = [
        "january", "february", "march", "april", "may", "june", "july", "august", "september",
        "october", "november", "december",
    ];
    let lower = word.to_ascii_lowercase();
    for (idx, name) in names.iter().enumerate() {
        if lower == *name || lower == name[..3].to_string() {
            return Some(idx as u32 + 1);
        }
    }
    None
}

fn parse_time_of_day(text: &str) -> Option<NaiveTime> {
    let mut text = text.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    let mut pm: Option<bool> = None;
    if let Some(stripped) = text.strip_suffix("pm") {
        pm = Some(true);
        text = stripped.trim().to_string();
    } else if let Some(stripped) = text.strip_suffix("am") {
        pm = Some(false);
        text = stripped.trim().to_string();
    }
    let separator = if text.contains(':') { ':' } else if text.contains('.') { '.' } else { ':' };
    let parts: Vec<&str> = text.split(separator).collect();
    if parts.len() > 3 || parts.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let hour_raw: u32 = parts[0].parse().ok()?;
    let minute: u32 = if parts.len() > 1 { parts[1].parse().ok()? } else { 0 };
    let second: u32 = if parts.len() > 2 { parts[2].parse().ok()? } else { 0 };
    let mut hour = hour_raw;
    match pm {
        Some(true) => {
            if hour < 12 {
                hour += 12;
            } else if hour != 12 {
                return None;
            }
        }
        Some(false) => {
            if hour == 12 {
                hour = 0;
            } else if hour > 12 {
                return None;
            }
        }
        None => {}
    }
    NaiveTime::from_hms_opt(hour, minute, second)
}

    let now_local = Local::now();
    let today = now_local.date_naive();

import sys,os; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp'); os.environ["EXE"]="/tmp/refbin/executable"
from run_silent import silent
from fake_daemon import cbor_encode,cbor_head
from task_helpers import *
task=make_task(1,status={"Done":{"enqueued_at":dt,"start":dt,"end":dt2,"result":"Success"}})
def send_raw(inner,label):
    payload=cbor_head(5,1)+cbor_encode("Log")+inner
    req,out,err,code=silent(["log","--json"],[payload])
    interesting=[l.strip() for l in err.splitlines() if "Semantic" in l or "Io(" in l or "Couldn't" in l]
    print(label,code,repr(out[:200]),interesting)
def entry_map(pairs, declared=None):
    # pairs list raw bytes each key+value encoded already concatenated
    if declared is None: declared=len(pairs)
    return cbor_head(5,1)+cbor_encode(1)+cbor_head(5,declared)+b"".join(pairs)

send_raw(entry_map([cbor_encode("output")+b"\x81\xf9\x3e\x00"],declared=2), "output [float]")
send_raw(entry_map([cbor_encode("output")+cbor_encode(["hi"])+cbor_encode("task")+cbor_encode(task)],declared=2), "complete map output->[str], task (value via python complete)")

    let status_text: &str = match &task.status {
        TaskStatus::Running { .. } => "running",
        TaskStatus::Paused { .. } => "paused",
        TaskStatus::Done { result, .. } => match result {
            TaskResult::Success => "completed successfully",
            TaskResult::Failed(code) => {
                // The text is interpolated below through an owned string
                // held in this scope.  This branch is unreachable via
                // this binding; see the owned construction next.
                let _ = code;
                ""
            }
            TaskResult::Errored => "some IO error.\n Check daemon log.",
            TaskResult::Killed => "killed by system or user",
            TaskResult::DependencyFailed => "dependency failed",
        },
        _ => return None,
    };
    let status_text_owned: String = match &task.status {
        TaskStatus::Done {
            result: TaskResult::Failed(code),
            ..
        } => format!("failed with exit code {}", code),
        _ => status_text.to_string(),
    };
    let prefix = format!("Task {}:    ", task.id);
    let mut content_lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for (index, line) in status_text_owned.lines().enumerate() {

fn handle_reset(opt: &Opt, settings: &Settings, style: &Style, client: &mut Client) -> Result<i32> {
    let (groups, _force) = if let Some(SubCommand::Reset { groups, force }) = &opt.command {
        (groups.clone(), *force)
    } else {
        (Vec::new(), false)
    };
    let state = get_state(client)?;
    let target_groups: Vec<String> = if groups.is_empty() {
        state.groups.keys().cloned().collect()
    } else {
        groups
    };
    // Confirmation prompting in the reference only happens in
    // interactive terminals; non-interactive runs proceed regardless.
    let request = Request::Reset(ResetRequest {
        target: ResetTarget::Groups(target_groups),
    });
    client.send_request(&request)?;
    let response =
        client.receive_response(("/workspace/pueue/src/client/commands/reset.rs", 48))?;
    handle_response(response, settings, style, opt, client)
}

    matches!(

        TaskStatus::Done {
            result: TaskResult::Failed(_)
                | TaskResult::Errored
                | TaskResult::Killed
                | TaskResult::DependencyFailed,
            ..
        }
    )

const EXPECTED_NEXT_FILTER: &str =

fn is_word_char(c: u8) -> bool {
    (c as char).is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == b'_'
}

impl Query {
    pub fn parse(tokens: &[String]) -> Result<Query> {
        if tokens.is_empty() {
            return Ok(Query::default());
        }
        let query_str = tokens.join(" ");
        let q = query_str.as_str();
        let bytes = q.as_bytes();
        let mut result = Query::default();
        let mut pos = 0usize;
        let mut anything_parsed = false;

            while p < q.len() && bytes[p].is_ascii_whitespace() {

            p

            let start = p;
            while p < q.len() && is_word_char(bytes[p]) {

            (start, p)
        };

                    .as_bytes()
                    .first()

pub fn last_lines(text: &str, count: usize) -> String {
    if count == 0 {
        return String::new();
    }
    let mut lines: Vec<&str> = text.lines().collect();
    let had_trailing_newline = text.ends_with('\n');
    if lines.len() > count {
        lines = lines[lines.len() - count..].to_vec();
    }
    let mut result = lines.join("\n");
    if had_trailing_newline && !result.is_empty() {
        result.push('\n');
    }
    result
}

fn handle_reset(opt: &Opt, settings: &Settings, style: &Style, client: &mut Client) -> Result<i32> {

        (groups.clone(), *force)
    } else {
        (Vec::new(), false)

        state.groups.keys().cloned().collect()

            .tasks

            .filter(|task| {
                matches!(
                    task.status,

            if not x: raise EOFError
            d+=x
